oracle.description: This JSON file is the single normative CLI command outcome, output destination, and process-exit authority. The design, decisions, and coverage Markdown files are checked views. If prose conflicts with this file, this file wins.
oracle.scope: CLI presentation and process termination after command parsing, shared request validation, shared-client execution, or a raw stream; no operation, HTTP, storage, workflow, or remote-effect semantics are created here.
oracle.compatibilityRule: Within v1, an existing semantic kind, error-code mapping, output destination, framing rule, or numeric exit cannot change. Additive operation applicability may select an already registered semantic kind. A new semantic kind or changed number requires a new oracle version and migration note.

terminology.meaning: A process-agnostic validated value, raw stream, or failure before any process exit is chosen.
A registered machine meaning selected from validated data or a registered error. It never contains a number or output destination.
A successfully transported and validated domain value that requires operator or agent attention and therefore exits nonzero without becoming a transport error.
The command value on stdout: one structured line, human frames, or exact raw bytes. Diagnostics are never primary output.
At least one requested stdout or stderr byte was accepted, or a started write cannot prove zero acceptance, before non-EPIPE completion failure. Every prefix remains observable and is never retried.
A PublicErrorEnvelope validated against the shared HTTP registry or the exact operation-scoped definition and status authority.

requirements.text: One strict process-agnostic result algebra separates validated values, raw streams, registered failures, and runtime termination events.
Every semantic kind has exactly one stable numeric exit owned only by the central registry; 126, 127, and 128+signal conventions remain reserved.
JSON, human, and raw modes have exact stdout/stderr destinations and deterministic framing with no cross-context transformation.
Every current client, shared, and operation-scoped error maps without message parsing; unregistered or malformed errors fail as protocol errors, never success.
HTTP-200 registered errors and action, doctor, routing, or sync attention values retain their domain meaning and request nonzero exits where specified.
Raw stdout is byte-exact, backpressured, never sanitized, never mixed with diagnostics, never retried after any accepted byte, and truthfully classifies EPIPE and partial completion.
SIGINT and SIGTERM request one awaited idempotent cleanup path, suppress new output and stacks, and settle to 130 and 143; EPIPE settles to 141.
Structured and human failures retain safe correlation IDs, suppress stack/cause/credential material, and use bounded registered projections.
Feature adapters may select only operation-applicable registered semantic kinds and cannot supply numbers, destinations, process streams, or private error maps.
Constructive matrices and a drift checker reconstruct all accepted operations, client kinds, shared errors, operation error rows, domain branches, and runtime branches.
Issue 214 and every blocked CLI, admin, parity, acceptance, and security contract have exact consumption and proof obligations.

planningShieldApplicability.reason: The oracle pins the accepted commit, source digests, issue evidence, and precedence.
The manifest separates client, domain, renderer, sink, signal, and process-termination seams.
This policy owns no durable write or read-back value.
This policy records no external effect in local persistence.
Raw streaming, cancellation, signals, terminal arbitration, and cleanup form an explicit protocol.
No recoverable product state is created or restored by this seam.
JSON/human/raw and direct REST/composed CLI behavior require one parity authority.
Sink fakes must retain partial writes, backpressure, EPIPE, errors, cancellation, and cleanup shapes.
Raw streams and slow sinks require bounded memory and progress-aware deadlines.
Mail, filenames, links, errors, diagnostics, correlation values, and terminals cross trust boundaries.
Stable exits and truthful operator output are public CLI usability contracts.
This artifact is specified design; implementation and composed proof remain separate downstream evidence.

commandResultAlgebra.boundary: Parse every candidate from unknown. Reject unknown keys. Operation data must already be validated by the shared operation registry. Human segments must carry the accepted output-context brands.
commandResultAlgebra.registeredErrorPrecedence: Before an operation-specific value classifier, a value shaped as a public error envelope must validate against the operation or shared error authority and use the registered error mapping. An envelope-like value with an unknown code or invalid details is protocol, never success.
commandResultAlgebra.unknownPrecedence: Missing semantic selection, an unregistered kind, a kind not allowed for the operation, a caller-supplied number, or a disagreement with a deterministic domain rule is protocol and exits 76. It can never default to success.

modeResolution.explicit: Exactly one syntactically recognized explicit context selects json, human, or raw before request validation; a later operation mismatch is reported in that selected context.
modeResolution.preCommandFailure: Before a command and one context can be resolved, use human failure output.

outputPolicy.jsonSuccess: Write JSON.stringify(validated data) followed by exactly LF to stdout. Write no success marker or error to stderr. A nonzero domain value remains on stdout.
outputPolicy.jsonFailure: Construct a fresh ErrorEnvelopeV1 in exact key order code,message,correlationId,details; write JSON.stringify(projection) plus exactly LF to stderr and zero stdout bytes. A server PublicErrorEnvelope retains the exact four validated values; local failures use a registered cli.* envelope and the invocation correlation ID.
outputPolicy.humanSuccess: Render only branded humanLines through renderHuman. The runner owns logical line separators and exactly one final LF. A nonzero domain value remains on stdout.
outputPolicy.humanFailure: Write exactly 'error[' + visible(code) + ']: ' + visible(message) + ' (correlation ' + visible(correlationId) + ')' plus LF to stderr through the human renderer. Do not render details or a stack.
outputPolicy.rawSuccess: After raw TTY preflight and optional diagnostic preflight, copy only stream bytes to stdout with awaited backpressure. Do not append LF, metadata, counts, progress, or a success marker.
outputPolicy.rawFailure: Before any accepted output byte, write one ErrorEnvelopeV1 JSON line to stderr. After a non-EPIPE partial or unknowable stdout/stderr write, preserve every accepted prefix, write cli.partial-output to stderr only when that sink remains writable, and exit 88. Its failedBoundary and two accepted-byte counts are the bounded snapshot taken when the terminal cause latches, before failure reporting. EPIPE and signals emit nothing further.
outputPolicy.diagnostics: Diagnostics are opt-in and capped at 16 records. JSON and raw modes construct strict DiagnosticV1 records in exact key order version,kind,level,code,message,correlationId,details and emit JSON.stringify(record) plus LF only on stderr; human mode emits branded human-safe lines only on stderr. Code/message/correlation/details are parsed from unknown, credential and stack-like keys are recursively forbidden, messages are at most 500 UTF-8 bytes, and encoded details are at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes. Pre-stream metadata diagnostics are completed before the first raw byte. There is no progress output.
outputPolicy.framing: One runner serializes writes per sink. JSON and diagnostic records are fully encoded before write and end in exactly one LF. A write-all loop awaits backpressure. Cross-sink observation order is not promised except that requested raw preflight diagnostics finish before the first raw byte. Unknown acceptance after a started write is conservatively partial.
outputPolicy.correlation: Retain an exact validated server correlationId for server errors. All locally synthesized envelopes use one validated invocation correlationId injected into the process-agnostic executor. Never replace a server ID or copy an exception string into it.
outputPolicy.stack: No JSON, human, raw diagnostic, usage, or fallback output may contain stack, cause, credentials, raw mail, arbitrary Error.message, or inspected exception objects.

outputDispositionMatrix.stderr: unchanged accepted prefix; no new output

executionProtocol.name: CliCommandEmissionV1
executionProtocol.owner: one command executor actor per process invocation
executionProtocol.receiptRule: For normal completion, semanticKind and exitCode are the exact exitCodeRegistry pair. The only exceptions are cancelled with 130 or 143 for SIGINT/SIGTERM and partial_output with 141 for EPIPE. Every other pair is invalid.
executionProtocol.cleanupReceiptRule: cleanupAwaited is true only after the memoized cleanup promise settled and false only when no cleanup path was registered or required. EPIPE, SIGINT, SIGTERM, caller abort, and an opened raw stream failure must settle cleanup before any receipt.

rules: The actor owns one AbortController, one stdout sink, one stderr sink, separate accepted-byte counters, one terminal-cause latch, and one memoized cleanup promise.
The first observed SIGINT or SIGTERM latches the signal terminal cause and outranks every non-signal cause. A later signal cannot change it.
EPIPE outranks non-signal client, sink, and cleanup failures but never outranks an already latched SIGINT or SIGTERM.

After any requested stdout or stderr byte, a non-EPIPE client, sink, render, diagnostic, or cleanup failure becomes partial_output. Unknown bytesAccepted after a started write is treated as partial_output.
Before any output byte, a sink failure becomes io; a render or cleanup invariant becomes internal; a client failure keeps its registered semantic kind.
A signal handler only records the event and requests abort. Cleanup and any process status decision happen in normal async execution.
No terminal branch retries a command, a remote operation, or an output prefix.
terminalPrecedence: partial_output after an accepted or unknown stdout/stderr prefix

safetyPolicy.human: Every feature-provided value remains UntrustedValue. Only fixed CLI chrome from trustedChrome may frame it. Runtime brands and exact keys are revalidated. Raw bytes never enter renderHuman.
safetyPolicy.structured: JSON preserves validated semantic values. It does not apply terminal escaping, truncation, display-width logic, color, or human sanitization.
safetyPolicy.raw: Raw bytes are copied exactly after TTY policy. Diagnostics and metadata use stderr only. No raw byte is decoded for classification or error parsing.
safetyPolicy.errors: Server error envelopes are validated by exact code, status, fixed message when defined, strict detail schema, and safe public envelope. Local errors use fixed messages and strict bounded safe detail shapes.
safetyPolicy.hostileContent: ESC, CSI, OSC, DCS, APC, PM, SOS, CR, backspace, C0/C1, DEL, bidi controls, combining marks, hostile filenames, URLs, error strings, and correlation values are inert in human mode and faithful JSON strings in structured mode.

rules: A feature adapter selects only a semanticKind string. The shape has no numeric, stream, destination, or renderer field.
The shared module validates the kind against exitCodeRegistry and the operation's valuePolicy, then recomputes deterministic domain rules when one exists. A mismatch is cli.protocol/76.
Registered public errors bypass feature selection and map centrally by code plus typed details. Messages and HTTP status alone never select a kind.
An additive operation mapping may reuse an existing kind only after adding exact operation applicability and proof. A new kind or changed meaning requires oracle v2.

Future routing replay, expiry, and tamper errors must first become registered strict operation/shared errors or strict domain discriminants. Their feature adapter may then select replay, expired, or tampered; it may not infer them from a private exception or message.

decisions.decision: Make semantic kind the only bridge from validated command meaning to one central numeric registry.
Use macOS sysexits values where their meanings fit and reserve Agent Mail 79 through 88 for required domain distinctions.
Never emit 124 through 127 or a normal semantic value above 127; use 130, 141, and 143 only for signal conventions.
Keep a validated HTTP-200 domain attention value on stdout while returning its nonzero semantic exit.
Map registered public errors by code and typed details, never by message text or status alone.
Treat an HTTP-200 registered error envelope as the same failure as its non-200 form.
Emit canonical JSON values on success and the exact four-field safe error envelope on stderr for failures.
Keep human success and attention on stdout, human errors on stderr, and pass all values through the accepted branded renderer.
Keep raw stdout byte-exact and require JSONL diagnostics on stderr when requested.
Use 141 and silence for EPIPE after awaited upstream cancellation, regardless of accepted-byte count.
Use partial_output 88 for every non-EPIPE failure after an accepted or unknowable stdout/stderr prefix and forbid retry.
Use 130 and 143 for SIGINT and SIGTERM after one awaited idempotent cleanup, with no new output or stack.
Retain exact server correlation IDs and synthesize local envelopes only from one injected invocation correlation ID.
Pair every fixed local code/message/semantic kind with one strict machine-readable bounded detail schema; never copy Error.message, stack, cause, credentials, or raw content.

Use ordered first-match action selectors: registered error, uncertainty/unknown-after-restore, partial, exact all-stale or invalidated, expired, inspect cancellation, exact operation success, then attention fallback.
Classify unhealthy/degraded doctor and authBlocked sync status as attention while preserving their validated value.
Validate feature semantic selections against declarative operation applicability and deterministic domain rules.
Keep missing routing replay/expiry/tamper discriminants as a downstream contract obligation instead of inventing CLI-private codes.
Default value operations to human and byte streams to raw; allow JSON/human only for values and raw only for bytes; reject a mismatch as usage before configuration/client execution.

implementationObligations.must: Implement the strict algebra, registries, value classifiers, local safe envelopes, sink abstraction, and process-agnostic receipt exactly.
Implement JSON/human/raw destinations, EPIPE/signals, terminal precedence, byte counting, and one awaited memoized cleanup path.
Execute every matrix row and property counterexample, including malformed selections, hostile values, partial writes, and signal races.
Reject direct process writes, console output, private numeric maps, caller exitCode, raw human sanitization, stack output, and retry after prefix.

Use success for committed and dry-run values, attention for a validated non-dry-run uncommitted label, and central registered mappings for expiry, replay, and tamper. Current routing operations expose no strict replay/expiry/tamper public discriminants; return that gap to the contract/route owner instead of parsing storage exceptions or inventing CLI codes.
Preflight TTY policy, write only exact bytes, await backpressure, cancel once, use 141 for EPIPE, 88 for other post-prefix failure, underlying mapping before bytes, and 130/143 for signals.

Retain every target result, certainty, approval state, and terminal audit and conform to the exact action rule precedence; no partial, all-stale, invalidated, expired, cancelled, unknown-after-restore, incomplete, uncertain, or other attention value may exit 0.
Require #214 before all five children and retain output/exit evidence per command without child-local policy.
Project validated status; authBlocked is attention 85 and all other accepted actor states are success 0. Do not infer state locally.
Map registered error envelopes equally at HTTP 200 or non-200, including typed stale-version/auth-blocked detail cases; accepted/completed actor-observed values are success.
Invalid query/cursor is 65; empty valid page is success; canonical JSON remains stdout and errors remain stderr.
Unknown/tombstoned-as-unavailable registered not_found is stderr and 66; known value is safely rendered on stdout.
Unknown is registered not_found/66; the accepted empty known continuation remains canonical stdout success/0; no thread-local number.
Emit success only after the validated verified artifact; any future operation_conflict must be registered and select conflict 79 centrally.
Preserve all findings; healthy exits 0 and degraded/unhealthy values remain stdout with attention 85.

Teach agent callers that a validated attention, partial, uncertain, stale, expired, or cancelled value remains on stdout with a meaningful nonzero exit; do not discard it as transport failure or infer success from parseable stdout alone.
Use raw stream semantics for exact JSONL bytes, JSONL diagnostics on stderr, 141 EPIPE, and 88 other post-prefix failure.
Compare canonical values, output destinations, and exits for every doctor/reindex/backup/restore success and failure cell.
Add success, registered error, client error, attention, partial, uncertain, and raw runtime cells with no unclassified operation.
Index the oracle/checker digest plus exact implementation, composed, capacity, security, and delivery evidence separately.
Run the oracle checker and checked-view digest verification from the frozen candidate without rewriting files; an oracle, view, source-inventory, or generated drift fixture must fail the gate.
Exercise full-scale raw and selected-export streams through slow and closed sinks; retain exact bytes, bounded memory, backpressure, terminal status, and zero leaked client/blob/sink resources.
Rerun the complete outcome/output/exit matrix against the frozen release candidate and final operation registry.
Exercise hostile human/error/diagnostic/correlation values, raw separation, stack suppression, malformed registered errors, and direct-write/private-exit bypass attempts.
Treat an omitted operation, false exit 0, wrong destination, unfaithful fake, cleanup race, or missing composed proof as a finding or explicit release gap; unit-green evidence cannot clear this seam.

Keep any #213/#214 output, exit, safety, or parity finding open until its original reproduction, faithful affected gate, adjacent counterexample, repair digest, and bounded repair-diff seam review all pass.

Execute documented commands with exact stdout, stderr, and exit assertions for success, domain attention, registered failure, and raw interruption; documentation must not flatten nonzero values or promise unsupported exits.

adjacentCounterexamples.mustFail: An unregistered or missing semantic kind falls through to exit 0.
A validated sync error envelope carried by HTTP 200 is printed as success.
A partial or uncertain action is summarized as success while targets disappear.
A completed action with missing or duplicate target result coverage exits 0.
Action inspect ignores cancelled, expired, invalidated, unknown-after-restore, or incomplete terminal authority and exits 0.
A progress, metadata, diagnostic, or newline byte is written to raw stdout.
A stream or operation is retried after stdout accepted any byte.
EPIPE emits a stack or human error line instead of silent 141 after cleanup.
SIGINT or SIGTERM runs cleanup twice or a later non-signal error replaces the signal status.
A correlation ID, message, filename, or URL can overwrite trusted human chrome.
A feature adapter provides exitCode, writes process streams, or defines a private numeric table.
Routing replay, expiry, or tamper is inferred by parsing an exception or error message.
